name: Name cross-period fluency as a development marker
text_content:
Type: structure

The record names one development marker, cross-strand fluency, makes it visible in the web as more connections, and recognizes it in compensation as meaningful. Everything else in the record requires a second one: one restaurant and one brand met at different times of day, late night as dinner's own later register, one system and four moods, same foundation and four registers, each period continuing the one before it. All of that asks the same person to hold a different register at a different hour, and the record names no marker for it and says nothing about whether it is recognized (finding 15.1, P62). It bears on recruiting because one labor pool staffs the periods, the seat sheet's service-period field is where a second period is recorded, and the first period expansion is the first succession event, so the dinner cohort is being hired into a fluency the record has not named. The structural element to finalize: cross-period fluency named as a development marker parallel to cross-strand fluency and recorded on the person page as connections. Whether it is recognized in compensation is Session 13's; its structural placement is Session 8's; both receive it as carryovers.

Filed by Session 5 of the Scaling People translation program. Session task 86ajgmhm4. Reasoning lives on the S5 page of the Sŏn Operating System doc 2ky45bmy-17253.

comment.text: Session 13 recognizes cross-period fluency in pay as a marker on the same mechanism as cross-strand fluency, on while the period connections are current inside the window, because a day counts once and the second register would otherwise earn nothing. The fluency record is read by the stack for the markers' currency and by the review as facts never scored; a lapsed window is told by the stack on the progression state and never by the lead at the review. S13 page, sections 8.2 and 10.3; P18, P29; readiness row 162.
